clue.text: Exactly what is needed in employment

definitions.meaning: an idiom for something perfectly suited to the purpose
read literally, someone holding a post is right in the work

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial way of praising an ideal fit, and literally describes being at work in a post.

clue.text: The babble of an injector

definitions.meaning: someone who jabs, as with a needle

explanation.definitionFit: Babble is meaningless chatter, the noun sense; and one who jabs a needle into skin is literally a jabber.

clue.text: Begin now when the TV is not on

definitions.meaning: to start out on a journey or task

definitions.text: when the TV is not on
definitions.meaning: a television set that is switched off

explanation.definitionFit: To start out on a trip is a phrasal-verb synonym for beginning; a television receiver is a set, and when unpowered it is off.

clue.text: Helping with great changes in signalling

indicators.note: the letters of the two words undergo changes, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone credits a helper with making big changes in how messages are sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the letters of HELPING and GREAT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending messages by wire or by visible gestures is a form of signalling.

clue.text: Before circling north, it swoops on its prey

indicators.note: the word for 'before' goes around, circling the letter for north

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A bird of prey circles northward before diving on its quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle is a raptor that dives down to seize fish.

clue.text: A sultry coo coming about as a result of the kissing

indicators.note: the phrase suggests the letters turning about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sultry coo arises as a result of some romantic kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming about' rearranges A, SULTRY and COO.
explanation.definitionFit: Osculation is the formal word for a kiss, and this adjective describes anything relating to kissing.

clue.text: Neither fore nor aft on ships?

definitions.text: Neither fore nor aft on ships?

parts.words: Neither fore nor aft on ships?
parts.note: a word that, joined to 'ships' in the clue, makes the nautical term for the middle part of a vessel

explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus SHIPS gives the sailor's word for the midpoint of a vessel, away from both bow and stern; alone it means 'in the middle of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the middle position on a vessel is being between its bow and stern.

clue.text: Union many single people enter into

definitions.text: Union many single people enter into

parts.words: Union many single people enter into
parts.note: describes the wedded state that unattached people commit to

explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is a union that unmarried people enter into.

clue.text: Blow up school in time!

indicators.note: the school is placed in the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A command to blow up a school at a set time.
explanation.definitionFit: To explode a bomb is to blow it up.

clue.text: Hold up not far from Cork!

definitions.meaning: the narrow part of a bottle sits right by its cork

explanation.definitionFit: A narrow point that slows traffic is a delay; the narrow top of a bottle lies next to its stopper.

clue.text: Work that causes worry?

parts.note: decorative openwork whose first word is also a verb meaning to be anxious

explanation.definitionFit: To be anxious is to worry, and the word also prefixes 'work' for ornamental lattice carving.

clue.text: Critical moment for a pivot

definitions.meaning: the point at which things decisively change
a fixed point around which something rotates

explanation.definitionFit: A decisive juncture is a watershed; literally, a pivot is the spot around which something swivels.

clue.text: Portrait of Guy!

parts.note: the stuffed figure of Guy Fawkes burnt on British bonfires each 5 November

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, a 'guy' is a model of Guy Fawkes burnt on Bonfire Night, 5 November.
explanation.definitionFit: A crude model or likeness of a person, like a guy for the bonfire, is a representation of them.

clue.text: It is not what it appears to be

definitions.text: It is not what it appears to be

parts.words: It is not what it appears to be
parts.note: describes a deceptive appearance or false perception

explanation.definitionFit: A false perception or deceptive appearance is something that misleads the eye.

clue.text: Amazed at not being prepared in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: not being prepared in a manner of speaking
definitions.meaning: read literally, without an address ready to give

explanation.definitionFit: Being dumbstruck with surprise leaves one wordless; literally, someone without an address prepared lacks an oration.

clue.text: One entitled to be trodden underfoot?…

definitions.text: One entitled to be trodden underfoot?…

parts.words: One entitled to be trodden underfoot?…
parts.note: a titled man named after floor covering that is walked on

explanation.walkthrough: The term is a derisive one for a man knighted for civilian service rather than on the battlefield; the clue reads it as a titled person who is walked over like a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour-holder who earned his title at court rather than in war is mocked with the name of a rug.

clue.text: Musical state…

definitions.meaning: a 1943 Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show
one of the fifty US states

explanation.definitionFit: Rodgers and Hammerstein's first stage show shares its title with the US state whose territory it portrays.

clue.text: … young lady, our one in America

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried young woman
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a girl described as our own American.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this to the clue before: 'state' carries over, so the definition is a state in America.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state lies on the Mississippi in the American Midwest.

clue.text: … and one behaving in quixotic fashion during darkness, we hear, and deviating from the norm

indicators.note: signals that a word for darkness is spoken and then written differently

parts.note: night is the time of darkness
errant means straying from the proper course

explanation.surface: Someone acts like Don Quixote in the dark and strays from accepted behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Quixote imagined himself a wandering chivalric hero, hence 'quixotic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes's hero Don Quixote set out as a wandering medieval adventurer seeking chivalrous deeds.

clue.text: Georgia went on the wagon and found half of 15 or 18

indicators.note: the second piece goes on after the first

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a wain is an old word for a farm wagon

explanation.surface: Someone from Georgia gave up drink and discovered something about knights.
explanation.walkthrough: Answers 15 and 18 are both six-six phrases ending in KNIGHT, so 'half of' either is that word; this is a knight of the Round Table. 'On the wagon' looks like teetotalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain is one of King Arthur's Round Table champions, so he is a chivalric warrior.

clue.text: Lady on the river had extra room

indicators.note: the down entry places one piece on top of the other

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
the Exe is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A woman living by the river had an additional room built.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension or outbuilding added on is an additional room or wing.

clue.text: Drink spilt in the basin

indicators.note: the letters are spilt out and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A glass of green spirit has been spilt into the washbasin.
explanation.definitionFit: The green wormwood spirit is an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: It is odds on a fall caused it

definitions.text: It is odds on a fall caused it

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
rain is a fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A bettor reckons a tumble was almost certainly behind the injury.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is a British horse-racing term for the odds at the off. Read whole, a tumble likely caused the wrenched joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrenched ankle or wrist is commonly the result of a tumble.

clue.text: Share only 50 per cent of the payment

indicators.note: only half of the word for a payment to shareholders is taken

parts.note: a dividend is a payment to shareholders

explanation.surface: Someone receives only half of what they were owed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of DIVIDEND is a British colloquial short form for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for a dividend, a shareholder's portion of profits.

clue.text: Spouse (not from London area) arranged musical work

indicators.note: the remaining letters are arranged afresh, as a composer arranges music
the London postcode letters are taken away from the spouse

parts.note: SE is the South East London postcode district

explanation.surface: A husband or wife from outside London arranged a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not from' removes SE from SPOUSE to leave POUS; 'arranged' reorders those four.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer's numbered composition is a piece of music.

clue.text: In the discussion, one student with sex-appeal will weaken

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed in the word for discussion

parts.note: a debate is a formal discussion
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: During a debate, an attractive student will sap the arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for sex appeal comes from the 1927 film It starring Clara Bow.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap strength or make feeble is to enfeeble.

clue.text: Revolutionary centre of the world

parts.note: the imaginary line through the poles that Earth rotates around

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics, but it means rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: The line through the poles about which the planet spins is its rotational centre.

clue.text: Support cases Stan and I moved

indicators.note: the letters are moved into a different order

explanation.surface: Stan and I moved some cases as a form of support.
explanation.definitionFit: Help or backing given to someone is support.
